region: Lodi · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Lamoreaux Landing farms the slopes above the eastern shore of Seneca Lake, where the Wagner family has grown grapes for three generations. Mark Wagner founded the winery in 1990 after taking over the family farm in 1978. Today it is run with his nephew Josh Wig, and winemaker Jesse Alexander makes every wine on site from the family’s own fruit. Riesling is the estate’s backbone, covering about half the vineyard, and its single-vineyard bottlings have drawn praise from Wine & Spirits and Wine Enthusiast.

The Riesling Ice Wine is the estate’s sweetest Riesling, made in small quantities and usually sold in half bottles. Ice wine depends on frozen grapes: the water in the berries is left behind as ice when they are pressed, so only a small amount of very concentrated, sugary juice runs off. Writer Jamie Goode, visiting the winery, noted that its Riesling Ice was frozen artificially after picking rather than on the vine. That makes it a more reliable wine to produce, with the same intense sweetness balanced by Riesling’s high natural acidity.

Critics have praised more recent vintages for keeping their balance despite the sweetness. VinePair gave the 2022 91 points for its pear, honey and orange peel, and James Suckling rated the 2024 94, noting apricot, marmalade and lively acidity. The 2019 shows golden raisin, apricot and honey, rich enough to stand in for dessert.
facts: Ice wine; very sweet, high acidity
Grapes frozen after harvest, then pressed (per Wine Anorak; confirm for 2019)
